name: Genetic Difference of Sex Development of Gynecological Interest
aliases: Disorders of Sex Development (DSD) with Gynecological Manifestations
Genetic Sex Development Variants Affecting Female Reproductive System

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Criteria for Diagnosis of Genetic Differences of Sex Development

criteria.description: Presence of chromosomal anomalies affecting sex chromosomes (e.g., mosaicism, structural abnormalities)
Abnormal serum levels of sex steroids or gonadotropins inconsistent with phenotypic sex
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in sex development pathways (e.g., SRY, SOX9, NR5A1)
Presence of atypical external genitalia or internal reproductive tract anomalies
Ultrasound or MRI evidence of gonadal dysgenesis or Müllerian duct anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chromosomal anomaly or pathogenic genetic variant plus abnormal hormonal profile consistent with sex development disorder
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including genetics, endocrinology, and gynecology.

pathognomonic.notes: Variable degrees of virilization or undervirilization
Absent or hypoplastic uterus and fallopian tubes

common.notes: Enlarged clitoris due to androgen exposure
Incomplete or delayed secondary sexual characteristics
Impaired fertility due to gonadal dysfunction

occasional.notes: Breast tissue development in phenotypic females or males
Emotional and psychological impact of DSD diagnosis

rare.notes: In cases with associated congenital adrenal hyperplasia
Associated with some genetic syndromes involving DSD

laboratory: Abnormal sex steroid hormone levels (e.g., testosterone, estradiol)
Elevated gonadotropins (LH, FSH) indicating gonadal dysgenesis
Karyotype analysis revealing sex chromosome anomalies
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing absent or hypoplastic uterus and gonads
MRI delineating internal reproductive tract anomalies
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SRY, SOX9, NR5A1, WT1, and other sex development genes
Copy number variations affecting sex determination loci
other: Histopathological confirmation of gonadal tissue type
Psychological assessment for gender identity and support

distinguishingFeatures: Normal to elevated testosterone with end-organ resistance
Absent Müllerian structures due to anti-Müllerian hormone effect
Enzyme deficiencies causing cortisol biosynthesis defects

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth requiring urgent evaluation
Delayed or absent puberty with primary amenorrhea
Rapid virilization or unexpected androgen effects
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Lee PA, et al. Global DSD update since 2006: management and research. Horm Res Paediatr. 2016.
Orphanet: Genetic difference of sex development of gynecological interest. Orphanet Report Series, 2023.
